answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 선정된 부분은 'where he worked as a freelance artist' 절 속의 관계부사절 구조입니다. 원문인 'where'를 관계대명사인 'which'로 오형 변형시킵니다. 'where' 뒤에 완전한 절(he worked as a freelance artist)이 오므로 관계부사가 적절하며, 'which'가 오면 불완전한 문장이어야 하므로 비문이 됩니다. 이는 선행사인 장소(Santa Fe)의 존재와 뒷문장의 완전성 여부를 확인해야 하는 관계사 핵심 어법 포인트입니다.

answer.surroundingText: Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, which he worked as a freelance artist.

answerStage.explanation: 밑줄 친 (B)가 포함된 절을 살펴보면 'he worked as a freelance artist'라는 완전한 구조의 문장이 이어지고 있습니다. 관계대명사 'which'는 선행사를 수식하면서 동시에 문장에서 주어나 목적어 역할을 겸해야 하므로 뒤에 불완전한 문장이 와야 합니다. 하지만 제시된 문장은 문장 성분이 모두 갖추어진 완전한 절이므로, 장소를 나타내는 선행사 'Santa Fe'를 수식하며 부사 역할을 하는 관계부사 'where'를 사용하는 것이 어법상 옳습니다.

question.explanation: 밑줄 친 (B)가 포함된 절을 살펴보면 'he worked as a freelance artist'라는 완전한 구조의 문장이 이어지고 있습니다. 관계대명사 'which'는 선행사를 수식하면서 동시에 문장에서 주어나 목적어 역할을 겸해야 하므로 뒤에 불완전한 문장이 와야 합니다. 하지만 제시된 문장은 문장 성분이 모두 갖추어진 완전한 절이므로, 장소를 나타내는 선행사 'Santa Fe'를 수식하며 부사 역할을 하는 관계부사 'where'를 사용하는 것이 어법상 옳습니다. 정답인 (B)를 제외한 나머지 보기들은 각 문장에서 요구하는 동사, 분사, 부사, 전치사구의 역할에 충실히 부합하는 문법적 구조를 갖추고 있습니다.

question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser __(A) created__ contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(B) which__ he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became __(C) interested__ in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet __(D) firmly__ rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, __(E) regardless of__ his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not __(A) to include__ in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(B) produced__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of __(C) its__ fantastical creatures. Both __(D) are__ useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences __(E) powerful__. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 대상 표현은 'struggle'이며, 이를 'struggling'이라는 분사구문/동명사 형태로 변형하여 오형을 만듭니다. 원문 구조는 'People (주어) who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail (관계사절) struggle (동사) to generalize... (부정사)'입니다. 이 문장에서 동사가 필요한 자리에 준동사를 넣으면 문장 전체가 동사 없는 구(phrase)가 되어 비문이 됩니다. 능동/수동이나 다른 문법 요소로 해석할 여지가 없는 완벽한 정동사 자리임을 반증 검사하여 확인했습니다.

answer.surroundingText: People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is.

question.passageWithMarkers: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break __(A) it__ up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode __(B) what__ we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more __(C) efficient__ way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail __(D) struggling__ to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of __(E) seeing__ the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 선택지 'seize'를 'seizing'으로 변형하여 문법적 비문을 생성함. 문맥상 'Why not + 동사원형' 구문을 묻는 의도이나, 동명사 형태로 바꾸어 동사원형의 병렬 구조를 파괴함. 'why not' 뒤에는 권유를 나타내는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 'seizing'은 명백한 오답임. 다른 선택지는 적절한 어법 포인트가 유지됨을 확인하여 반증 검사를 통과함.

answer.surroundingText: But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil.

answerStage.explanation: why not 뒤에는 동사원형이 오며 '~하는 게 어때?'라는 권유의 표현을 구성합니다. 해당 문장에서 'viewing'과 병렬 구조를 오해하도록 유도하는 전치사 뒤의 동명사형(seizing)을 썼으나, 문장 전체의 구조상 앞의 Why not에 호응하는 동사원형 seize가 와야 합니다. 따라서 seizing을 seize로 고쳐야 합니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

question.explanation: 이 문장은 'That'이 주어, 'is'가 동사이며, 뒤따르는 절이 주격 보어 역할을 하는 명사절의 구조를 띱니다. 명사절 내부의 주어 핵은 'the beauty', 동사구는 'comes into play'로 완전한 형태를 갖추고 있습니다. 보어 절을 이끌고 있으나 선행사가 없고, 뒤따르는 절이 빈자리 없이 완전하므로 대명사 역할을 하는 (B)의 which는 이 자리에 쓸 수 없습니다. 따라서 의미상 상황이나 장소를 나타내며 완전한 절을 이끄는 의문부사 또는 선행사가 생략된 관계부사 where로 고쳐야 합니다. 'comes into play'가 목적어를 필요로 하지 않는 완전한 일의적 관용구라는 점을 살펴야 풀 수 있습니다.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 문장 'Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment'에서 현재분사 'predicting'이 주어 'Your auditory areas'의 능동적 행위로서 적절히 사용됨을 확인했다. 대조군으로서 고정된 수동태 형태 'predicted'를 오형으로 배치하여, 과거시제의 정동사가 단독으로 올 수 없는 문법적 구조를 문제화했다. 다른 선지들과 함께 구조적 타당성을 검토했을 때, 이 오형은 주어와 동사의 관계 파악을 묻는 명백한 비문이다.

answer.surroundingText: Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention.

answerStage.explanation: 문장 내에서 'Your auditory areas'는 주어이고, 뒤에 이어지는 'moment after moment'와 함께 능동적인 예측 행위를 수행하고 있습니다. 따라서 과거형 동사인 predicted를 사용하면 뒤따르는 목적어 'its continuation'을 수식하거나 서술할 수 없고 문장 구조가 무너지게 됩니다. 주어의 능동적 동작을 나타내는 현재분사 predicting으로 쓰는 것이 옳습니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

question.passageWithMarkers: We have all had the experience of suddenly __(A) noticing__ that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 사역동사 'has'의 목적어 'us'와 목적격 보어의 관계가 능동이므로, 현재분사 'piling'을 쓰는 것이 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 전치사 'to'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 관계대명사 'what'은 불완전한 절을 이끌어 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 접속사 'While' 뒤에 주어와 be동사가 생략된 형태로 맥락상 능동의 의미를 지니므로 현재분사 'doing'이 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 'with + 명사 + 분사' 구문에서 'your phone'과 'press'의 관계가 수동이므로 과거분사 'pressed'가 옳습니다.

question.explanation: 주어 'The same' 다음에 이어지는 동사 자리에 자동사 apply가 와야 하는 구조입니다. 자동사는 수동태로 쓸 수 없으므로 'is applied'는 비문입니다. 따라서 'is applied'를 'applies'로 고쳐야 합니다. '적용되다'라는 우리말 해석 때문에 수동태로 착각할 수 있습니다.
keyPoints: (E) 능동태 vs 수동태 — 자동사 apply의 활용
(A) 분사의 능수동 — 목적어와 목적격 보어의 관계
(D) 분사의 능수동 — with 동시동작 구문의 분사 판단
question.passageWithMarkers: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us __(A) piling__ one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to __(B) what__ you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While __(C) doing__ the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone __(D) pressed__ to your ear. The same __(E) is applied__ to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 문장에서 'The moment that occurs'라는 부사절 구조를 타겟으로 선정했습니다. 'the moment' 뒤에 관계부사 'when'이나 관계대명사절을 이끄는 'that'이 생략된 구조여야 합니다. 이를 'every'로 변경하여 비문으로 설계했습니다. 'Every the moment'는 명사구 앞에 관사적 용법이 허용되지 않는 명백한 통사적 오류입니다. 다른 해석(분사구문 등)으로도 성립되지 않는 킬러 문항용 오답입니다.

answer.surroundingText: They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next.

answerStage.explanation: 밑줄 친 'Every the moment'는 명사구의 한정사 위치 오류입니다. 원문인 'The moment that occurs'는 '~하는 순간에'라는 의미의 부사구로 쓰인 경우이며, 접속사처럼 기능합니다. 반면 제시된 'Every the moment'는 관사와 한정사의 결합 순서가 어긋난 비문입니다. 정답은 'The moment'로 수정하여 관계절을 이끄는 선행사 역할을 하도록 해야 합니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주격 관계대명사 that이 단수 명사 'a critical factor'를 선행사로 받아 수식하므로 단수형 동사 'determines'를 쓴 것은 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 문맥상 펭귄들이 큰 무리를 지어 걷고 있는 진행의 느낌을 능동으로 나타내기 위해 현재분사 'strolling'을 보어로 쓴 것은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 선행사 'the leopard seal'을 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계대명사로서 주어 역할을 하는 'which'의 사용은 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): be동사 'is'의 주격 보어 역할을 하는 명사적 용법의 부정사 'to play'는 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장은 부사절 접속사 역할을 하는 표현을 요구합니다. 부사절(that occurs)과 주절(the rest of the penguins watch ~)을 연결하려면, 시간에 관한 부사절 접속사 역할을 하는 수거적 표현이 필요합니다. 'During the moment'는 전치사구에 불과하여 두 개의 절을 연결할 수 없는 비문입니다. 따라서 이것을 '그 일이 일어나는 즉시'라는 뜻의 접속사 역할을 하는 'The moment'로 고쳐야 합니다. 'During the moment'가 명사를 이끄는 전치사구임을 간과하면 오답으로 보기 어려울 수 있습니다.
keyPoints: (E) 전치사 vs 접속사 — 두 절을 연결하는 접속사 역할
(A) 수일치 — 주격 관계대명사절 동사의 선행사 수일치
(B) 분사의 쓰임 — 능동과 진행을 나타내는 현재분사 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: There is a critical factor that __(A) determines__ whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found __(B) strolling__ in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, __(C) which__ likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is __(D) to play__ the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. __(E) During the moment__ that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 선택한 정답 구문은 'not too much time goes by' 부분입니다. 여기서 수일치나 주어 판단을 묻기 위해 'goes'를 'go'로 변형하여 오류를 유발했습니다. 'time'은 불가산 명사로 단수 취급해야 하므로 'goes'가 정답이며, 'go'는 문법적으로 틀린 형태입니다. 이 오류는 주어-동사 수일치 개념을 명확히 테스트하며 문맥적으로 명백한 비문을 형성합니다.

answer.surroundingText: In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone

answerStage.explanation: 주어-동사 수일치 문제입니다. 해당 문장의 주어는 'not too much time'으로, 'time'은 셀 수 없는 추상명사이므로 항상 단수 취급합니다. 따라서 동사 자리에 복수형 동사인 'go'를 쓰는 것은 틀리며, 단수형인 'goes'가 적절합니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): tend to-v 구문으로, 'tend'의 목적어로 to부정사 'to go'가 오는 것은 자연스럽습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주격 관계대명사 that이 'the distance'를 선행사로 받아 has formed라는 현재완료 동사를 이끄는 구조가 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): people을 수식하는 관계사절 내에서 목적격 관계대명사가 생략된 구조이며, 주어 'we'와 'haven't spoken'은 수일치와 태 모두 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 이후의 시점을 나타내는 접속사 'since'로, 뒤에 주어+동사(you've spoken)가 이어지는 올바른 접속사 용례입니다.

question.explanation: 사역동사의 목적격 보어 자리를 묻는 문제입니다. 'let'은 사역동사이므로 목적어인 'yourself' 뒤에 목적격 보어로 동사원형이 와야 합니다. 따라서 'to fall'을 'fall'로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (E) 목적격 보어 — 사역동사 let 뒤의 동사원형
(A) to부정사 — 동사의 목적어로서의 to-v 형태
(B) 관계대명사 — 선행사와 일치하는 동사의 시제 및 수
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend __(A) to go__ long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance __(B) that has formed__ and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we __(C) haven't spoken__ to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while __(D) since__ you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself __(E) to fall__ out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.

passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.
